summary:
Held 0 of today's 10 biggest UK/EU movers.

• 6 upside misses — CAP.PA +9%, HEI.DE +3%, WPP.L +2%, IHG.L +2%, BP.L +2%. These cleared the universe screen but no strategy picked them up; the morning brief either filtered them on a catalyst/RSI/earnings rule or had nothing positive to trigger an entry.

• 4 downside moves (GAW.L -7%, NWG.L -6%, BAYN.DE -5%, BGEO.L -5%) are unreachable on a long-only basket — no mechanism to express a short or pair-trade.

• Most instructive miss: CAP.PA (+8.81%) — Accenture's beat (Q4 FY26 revenue +7% cc, orders $22.2B; ADR ~+17%) lifted IT-services peers. Capgemini hit an 8-month high, though sources date the main +7% jump to Oct 1, not Oct 2. Why we passed: Outside any active strategy's universe: CAP.PA is a CAC 40 large-cap IT-services name that no strategy covers. The move was a peer-earnings read-through that gapped at the open, so a post-open momentum signal would have come too late.

top_movers.catalyst: Accenture's beat (Q4 FY26 revenue +7% cc, orders $22.2B; ADR ~+17%) lifted IT-services peers. Capgemini hit an 8-month high, though sources date the main +7% jump to Oct 1, not Oct 2.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: CAP.PA is a CAC 40 large-cap IT-services name that no strategy covers. The move was a peer-earnings read-through that gapped at the open, so a post-open momentum signal would have come too late.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a peer-earnings read-through trigger: when a mapped US peer (e.g. ACN) gaps ≥+5% after results, add its European comps (CAP.PA, etc.) to the news-reactive universe at the next EU open with a gap-chase cap of ~+3%.

top_movers.catalyst: No obvious news catalyst. Only routine buyback disclosures and analyst notes (e.g. a UBS target cut) turned up, so this looks like a technical or sector move in European building materials/cyclicals.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: HEI.DE is a large-cap German (DAX) building-materials name that no strategy's universe includes. With no discrete catalyst, a news-reactive filter would also have had nothing to trigger on.
top_movers.suggestion: Add DAX/Stoxx 600 large-cap cyclicals (HEI.DE, etc.) to the momentum universe, gated by a ≥+2% close-to-close move with volume ≥1.5× its 20-day average, so sector-driven moves without news are caught.

top_movers.catalyst: No clear same-day catalyst found. Search turned up only a BlackRock 5.16% major-holdings filing, a CFO departure (to Diageo) and FTSE index reshuffle chatter. Likely a rebound or technical move.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: WPP is a UK mid/large-cap advertising stock that no strategy lists. With no earnings or M&A trigger, a +2.18% drift also wouldn't pass a news-reactive or gap-up filter.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a low-priority 'broad-liquidity' scan that admits FTSE 100/250 names into the momentum universe when the daily move is ≥ +2% on volume ≥ 1.5× the 20-day average, so unlisted mid-caps can qualify without a hand-maintained list.

top_movers.catalyst: No obvious news catalyst. The only IHG item found was routine buyback disclosures (1,000 shares repurchased 1 Oct), so this looks like a sector or technical move in UK travel and leisure.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe. IHG.L is a FTSE 100 large-cap hotel operator that no strategy lists. A +2.08% drift with no news and no volume spike would also likely fail momentum, gap and news-reactive triggers.
top_movers.suggestion: Add FTSE 100 consumer-discretionary and travel names such as IHG.L to the uk-eu mean-reversion/momentum universe, and keep the existing gap ≥ X% and volume ≥ 1.5× average filters so no-news drifts are still skipped.

top_movers.catalyst: Follow-through from the Wells Fargo upgrade to Overweight (target raised to $57) on deleveraging and rising EPS estimates ahead of Oct 30 results. BP rose despite Brent falling ~2.6%, so it looks like a stock-specific re-rating.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: BP.L is a UK large-cap integrated oil major that no strategy includes. The +1.7% move was a modest analyst-upgrade drift against falling crude, so it would not have tripped a gap or momentum trigger.
top_movers.suggestion: Add large-cap LSE energy names (BP.L, SHEL.L) to the news-reactive universe, with a trigger on broker upgrades that lift a name ≥1.5% while Brent is down. Alternatively, no action: the move was small and the signal weak.

top_movers.catalyst: No obvious news catalyst found. Search returned only generic quote pages, nothing specific to 2026-10-02. Likely a technical or sector rebound in UK software/large-cap names.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: SGE.L is a FTSE 100 large-cap software/accounting name that no strategy includes. A +1.56% move with no catalyst is also too small for gap-up or momentum triggers.
top_movers.suggestion: (no actionable change — a +1.56% move without a catalyst is below typical momentum thresholds; adding FTSE 100 software names to the universe isn't justified by a single day's move.)

top_movers.catalyst: No confirmed driver. Searches show GAW.L gapping down about 5.8% at the open, with a headline 'falls despite record year' that I couldn't tie to today. One source shows a partial intraday recovery.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: GAW.L is a UK mid/large-cap consumer discretionary name that no strategy lists. A gap-down at the open would also fail gap and RSI filters, and the bot has no short capability.
top_movers.suggestion: Add FTSE 100/250 consumer-discretionary names like GAW.L to the uk-eu mean-reversion universe, with a gap-down ≥5% watch rule that requires volume ≥1.5× the 20-day average before entry.

top_movers.catalyst: Sell-off in UK bank shares as global bond yields rose, plus profit-taking after a strong run. No NWG-specific news was found. Sources dated the drop to Oct 1, so the match to the Oct 2 close is unconfirmed.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: NWG.L is a large-cap UK bank that no strategy lists. The drop was a macro, rates-driven sector move with no stock-specific catalyst. A long-only momentum or news-reactive bot has no signal to buy it and cannot short it.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a sector-level 'UK banks drawdown' flag (e.g. NWG.L, LLOY.L, BARC.L down >4% together) to a mean-reversion strategy's universe, gated on no company-specific news. Alternatively accept this as a no-op, since the bot is long-only.

top_movers.catalyst: Bayer fell ~5% on a JPMorgan note saying Q3 consensus (results due 3 Nov) is too high, plus a new Roundup/glyphosate trial and mRNA patent claims. Some of the search results may refer to 1 Oct.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: BAYN.DE is a German large-cap pharma/agro name that no strategy includes. The drop was a gradual analyst-downgrade and litigation sell-off, not a clean gap or momentum signal, so the filters wouldn't have flagged it anyway.
top_movers.suggestion: Add large-cap DAX/EuroStoxx names like BAYN.DE to the news-reactive strategy's watch universe, with a trigger on analyst-cut or litigation headlines plus a ≤-4% daily move; the bot has no short capability, so this would only be a signal.

top_movers.catalyst: No company-specific news found. Lion Finance Group (ex-Bank of Georgia) fell in a broad UK bank sell-off on bond-market worries. Search showed -2.5% against the -5.01% close, so the cause is only partly explained.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe. It is a Georgia-focused frontier-market bank, mid-cap on the LSE, that falls outside the large-cap UK/EU lists. A sector or rates-driven drop with no stock-specific signal would not trigger news-reactive filters anyway.
top_movers.suggestion: (no actionable change) The drop looks sector or rates-driven and the bot is long-only. If wanted, add a UK-banks sector-drawdown flag using a ≥3% one-day basket move, rather than adding frontier-market names to the universe.
